title: Pair count computation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\\{0,1\\}$, let $g$ map finite bit strings to finite bit strings, and let $T : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every bit string $x$, $M$ computes $g(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps. Then the constructed machine computes, on every $x$, the one-bit output that is $1$ exactly when the pair parser succeeds with second component $b$ satisfying $|b| \\le |g(x)|$, and is $0$ otherwise, within $T(|x|)+2|x|+5$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$g$ maps bit strings to bit strings
$T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
$M$ computes $g(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps for every bit string $x$
